- **Database:** one SQLite file, `agent-hud.db`, sits in `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`, or in the state dir when that variable is not set. The `boards` table is `STRICT` and has one row per board, with its `BoardState` as JSON text.
- **Engine setup:** `open_database` sets `foreign_keys = ON` and `journal_mode = WAL` in a `connect` event, then runs Alembic to the latest schema. Alembic autogenerates the migration from the models.
- **Source of truth:** the database alone holds the board state and answers which boards exist. Each tool and socket loads the state in its session, applies the pure `BoardState` rule, and commits with `commit_board_state`. `act_on_board` does this for actions and wakes the board's watchers.

- **`Exchange`:** keeps only live state: the open monitors, the working flag and the change events. It is made the first time a board is used. Each open monitor gets each sent turn, and a turn leaves the state once every open monitor has had it.
- **Queries:** `queries/boards.py` has verb_noun functions over a `Session`. The tools get their session through FastMCP `Depends`.
- **Reads:** `read_changes` returns what changed since the agent's last read and moves the cursor forward, and `read` resets the cursor. `read`'s `since` is removed.
- **Removed:** the action log, the checkpoint, compaction, the agent position, the file lock and the one-file-per-board directory.

Part 3 of the stack that splits Mason-Levyy/myfitnesspal-mcp#33, as asked in [the review on Mason-Levyy/myfitnesspal-mcp#33](https://github.com/Mason-Levyy/myfitnesspal-mcp/pull/33#issuecomment-6226013744). **Based on part 1** (#54), because logging goes through `log_exact` and reports `added_entries`. Opened as a draft against `main` because GitHub can't base a PR on a fork branch, so the diff shows part 1's commit too until #54 merges; I'll rebase and mark it ready then.

## Summary

Custom foods, saved meals and recipes never show up in food search, so there was no way to log them.

- **`fitness_list_custom`** lists them with ids, servings and nutrition; meals list their ingredients.
- **`fitness_log_custom`** logs one by name. A saved meal logs as its ingredients, as on the website.

Loggable `food_id`/`weight_id` pairs come from the legacy "Add Food to Diary" tabs (GET `/food/load_*`). Nutrition and ingredients come from `/api/services/users/{foods,meals}/mine` and v2 `/recipes`, best effort, with an entry in `warnings` when they fail.

### Review items addressed

From [the review](https://github.com/Mason-Levyy/myfitnesspal-mcp/pull/33#issuecomment-6226013744):

- **Name-keyed id lookup.** `foods/mine` shares no id with the tabs (its `id` is not the tab's legacy `food_id`), so I can't join on an id. Details now join on the item's exact display name: `Brand - Name` for a branded food, `Name` for an unbranded one, one key each. "Oats" no longer gets "Quaker - Oats"' details. When several items share a display name, they all get no details and no id, and `warnings` names them. Tests cover both cases; the first fails on the old code.
- **`DiarySignedOut` instead of `NotLoggedIn`.** A redirect from a tab raises `diary.DiarySignedOut`, which `is_auth_error` matches by type.
- **Shared request plumbing.** `clean()` is gone in favour of `entry_matching.collapse_whitespace`. `api_url`, `json_headers` and `get_with_retry` live in `mfp_web.py`; `measurements.py` now uses the first two too.
- **Retrying HTTP 400s.** `get_with_retry` retries only 429 and 5xx. A test checks that a 400 is not retried. If the sporadic 400 on v2 `/recipes` comes back, it now shows up in `warnings`, and names and ids still work.
- **One serving matcher.** `custom_items.matching` is the one exact-then-partial matcher, for item names and serving names. A partial match must be unique; otherwise the error lists the choices. Part 4 reuses it for recipe ingredients.

With `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS` and `JSON_DIAGNOSTIC_POSITIONS`, the exceptions of `basic_json_view` now carry the same context as those of `basic_json`: `(/path) ` and `(bytes a-b) ` in front of the message, in `basic_json`'s format (with `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS`, no context for the root value). Until now, views threw without any context. Since #5922/#5923, `get<T>()` reads the view directly, so conversions had also lost the relative path they used to get through `materialize()`. This follows up the sketch discussed in #5864.

```
view, before: [json.exception.type_error.302] type must be number, but is string
view, now:    [json.exception.type_error.302] (/people/2/age) (bytes 83-86) type must be number, but is string
json:         [json.exception.type_error.302] (/people/2/age) (bytes 83-86) type must be number, but is string
```

## How

- **Throw sites.** The throw helpers in `detail/view/errors.hpp` take an `error_site` (document and node), which is empty without the two macros. All call sites pass the value `basic_json` would pass as context: accessors, `at()`/`operator[]`/`value()`, JSON pointers, conversions, and the edit functions.
- **Path.** Nodes have no parent index, so the path is found only when an exception is thrown, by descending from the root. Before the first edit, only the subtree that contains the value is searched (by subtree extent). After edits, the walk goes through the edited sequences.
- **Bytes.** Taken as `materialize()` sets them (`position_source`): a container ends where the chain of its last elements ends, plus a scan to the closing brackets. A value has bytes exactly when `materialize()` would give it positions.
- **`from_json()` and the strict enum macro.** For views, these put the same context in front of the message through a new `exception_prefix(j)` in `exceptions.hpp`. The `exception` class is unchanged.
- **Unchanged cases.** Array-index errors in JSON pointers stay without context, as in `json_pointer`. `key()` of an iterator over an array or a primitive (`invalid_iterator.207`) also stays without context: a view iterator does not know its container, and keeping it made a walk 1.1 % slower. This is documented.

## Performance

No cost on the success path. Instruction counts, B/A vs. develop, from the A/B harness (one binary, alternating samples, 6 code layouts). The workload walks twitter/citm/canada with range-for and `items()`/`key()`, plus `get<std::vector<double>>` and `at()`/`[]` lookups:

| | without the macros | `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS` | `JSON_DIAGNOSTIC_POSITIONS` |
|---|---|---|---|
| GCC 13, x86-64 (callgrind) | 0.9999–1.0000 | walks 1.0000, get 1.0042, lookup 1.0077 | same |
| clang, arm64 | 0.9993–1.0001 | 0.9990–1.0010 | 0.9995–1.0013 |

- **Code without the macros:** the view accessors compile to the same code as on develop.
- **GCC regression found and fixed.** A first version made GCC 13 stop inlining a recursive view walk into itself under the macros (2.7× the instructions). The path and byte code was instantiated in every translation unit, through non-template helpers, and that changed GCC's early inlining of unrelated view functions. The helpers that take an `error_site` are now templates, so this code is instantiated only where an exception can be thrown.
- **Cost of an exception:** with the macros, building the message takes time linear in the size of the document, only when an exception is thrown. This is documented.

## Tests

- **New:** a test compares every value's exceptions with those of the parsed or materialized `basic_json` value. It covers generated documents, comments and trailing commas, escaped keys (`~`, `/`, `\^@`), edited documents (against `materialize()`), and duplicate keys.
- **Re-enabled:** the comparisons with `json` that were disabled under the two macros run again.
- **Exact messages:** checks against fixed strings now build the expected message with `json_view_test::message(...)`, so they are exact under every macro combination.
- **Local runs:**
  - The json_view tests pass with ASan/UBSan under no macro, each macro alone, and both.
  - The full suite passes without the macros.
- **Not related to this PR:** with both macros at once, 8 `json`-only tests fail on develop as well (custom key types, `json_patch`, `json_pointer`, regression1). Their expected strings assume one macro at a time.

## Breaking changes

None. Messages change only when `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS` or `JSON_DIAGNOSTIC_POSITIONS` is enabled, and `json_view` first ships in 3.13.0. Without the macros, all messages and the generated code of the view accessors are unchanged.

Stacked on twentyhq/twenty#29368. This is the migration of the "AI runs without hidden agents" design: every builder AI step carried a hidden agent, and this moves that agent's config into the step. Deleting the agents comes in a follow-up command one release later (see below).

## What changes

A 2.55 workspace command, `upgrade:2-55:inline-workflow-step-agents`. Per workspace:

- **Which agents.** Step agents are the `isSystem` agents of the workspace Custom application that have no triggers. Only the builder creates those. An installed application's system agents are its own and are left alone.
- **What the step gets.** Each `AI_AGENT` step on a step agent receives:
  - `instructions`: the agent's prompt;
  - `modelId`, plus `modelConfiguration` reduced to the native tools' `enabled` flags;
  - the agent's response format, only when it is json and the step has none;
  - a `scope` built from the agent-only role: its explicit object and field rows, its permission flags, and `canAccessAllTools` / `canUpdateAllSettings`, by universal identifier. An agent with no role gives no scope, so the step still has no data tools, as today.
  
  `agentId` is dropped.
- **The role's all-records flags stay out of the scope.** Today a step agent's database tools reach only the objects its role grants row by row, intersected with the caller, whatever its all-records flags. A scope's all-records flag would name every object and give a step tools it never had. Keeping only the explicit rows preserves today's access.
- **Where.**
  - Core and workspace `workflowVersion.steps`.
  - The steps of runs that can still run one: not started, enqueued, running, and failed, since a failed run can be retried.
  - The run specs of paused workflow steps in `core."pendingWakeUp"`. A paused step's run spec becomes `{ agentId: null, inlineConfig }`, keyed `workflow-step:<stepId>` and run under the agent's application, so it continues with the config it paused with.
  
  Every rewrite is compare-and-set, as in `2-50/wrap-bare-select-filter-values`.
- **Not converted.** A role with row-level predicates can't be expressed as a scope. Its agent and steps stay as they are, and each step is logged with its workspace.
- **Dry run and reruns.** Dry run counts and writes nothing. A second run finds nothing to inline.

## Conversational steps keep their agent (Generate vs Agent)

An `AI_AGENT` step is either a **Generate** step (no `agentId`, inline config, one-shot: no conversation, no human input, no waiting) or an **Agent** step (has an `agentId`; the only kind allowed human input instructions or a `conversation` setting). twentyhq/twenty#29368 is gaining validation that rejects human input or `conversation` on a step without an `agentId`, so inlining such a step would make it invalid. The command therefore:

- **Leaves conversational steps on their agent.** A step whose `humanInputInstructions` is non-blank, or that has a `conversation` setting, keeps its `agentId` and is not inlined. Blank human input instructions don't count, matching the runtime, which trims them.
- **Makes that agent visible.** It sets `isSystem = false`, which is the flag that marks hidden step agents. It also renames the agent to `<workflow name> · <step name>` when its label was the generated `Workflow Agent xxxx` or was empty. A label someone wrote is kept.
- **Keeps it out of the deferred deletion.** The follow-up deletes `isSystem` step agents, so a visible agent no longer matches. A rerun no longer sees it as a step agent either.
- **Applies the same rule to paused runs.** A paused run stays on its agent when its run's step is conversational, or when its run spec can ask humans, which only human input instructions enable. Its agent is made visible too.
- **Inlines every other step** exactly as before, even one that sits next to a conversational step in the same workflow.

## Deleting the agents: a follow-up, one release later

This command deletes nothing:
- A `RunAgentJob` queued before the upgrade still holds `spec.agentId`. If its agent were deleted before a worker picks the job up, the step would fail.
- A later version's command will delete the step agents nothing references any more, together with their role targets, and then their agent-only roles. That includes the orphans that deleting a workflow or discarding a draft left behind. Agents this command made visible are no longer `isSystem`, so they are not candidates.
- It will do the role deletion in the same flat-entity migration call, rather than with raw SQL.
- It can't be registered yet, because only the current version's folder takes new commands.

Nothing this command does is irreversible: every step and wake-up keeps working through the runtime of twentyhq/twenty#29368, whichever shape it has.

## Ordering
- **No deploy fence.** The runtime from twentyhq/twenty#29368 runs both agent-backed and inline steps, so a workspace the command hasn't reached yet keeps working.
- **Ships with the builder PR.** The builder and editor switch-over (twentyhq/twenty#29371) lands first, so after the upgrade the step panel and AI tools edit inline steps.
- **Finished runs keep their `agentId`.** Completed and stopped runs are only displayed.

## Tests
- Unit tests for the command-only helpers (21 tests):
  - role → scope, including all-records flags left out;
  - inlining steps: response format precedence, no scope without a role, kept agents, already-inlined steps;
  - conversational steps: human input and a conversation keep the agent, a blank human input is still inlined, a plain step next to a conversational one is still inlined;
  - the visible agent's label;
  - native tool normalization;
  - paused run spec rewrite, including runs on a conversational step or able to ask humans staying on their agent.
- `tsgo` and oxlint are clean.
- Not run here: no Postgres was available, so neither the SQL nor an integration spec against a database ran.

Third PR of "AI runs without hidden agents", stacked on twentyhq/twenty#29368. The builder stops creating a hidden agent for each AI step. A new step holds its own instructions, model, model options and permission scope, which #29368 taught the runtime to run.

## Two step kinds

An `AI_AGENT` step is stored with the same type either way, but comes in one of two kinds:
- **Generate step** (no `agentId`): the step owns its instructions, model, model options, response format and permission scope. It runs once as the caller, with no conversation, no human input and no waiting.
- **Agent step** (`agentId` set): the agent owns its instructions, model and permissions. The step gives the prompt, plus optional human input instructions and a conversation setting.

**Picker** (`SidePanelWorkflowSelectAction`)
- The AI section offers one **Generate** item (sparkles icon). Steps the builder creates without an agent are now named "Generate".
- An **Agents** section lists each agent as its own item, labelled with the agent's name, the same way logic functions are flattened today.
- Only agents that are active, not system, and have a JSON response format with at least one field are listed, so the step has a known output schema. Agents without one are not offered, but existing steps that point at them keep working.
- Picking an agent sends `defaultSettings: { input: { agentId } }`. The builder then creates `{ agentId, prompt: '' }`, names the step after the agent, and derives the output schema from the agent's response format.

**Step editor**
- A Generate step shows the prompt, instructions, model and model options, output fields and the Permissions tab. It hides human input and conversation.
- An agent step shows the agent (a chip linking to it), the prompt, human input and conversation. It hides instructions, model, output fields and the Permissions tab.
- Legacy steps that run a hidden step-owned agent (`isSystem`) keep their current editor until the migration inlines them.

## What changes

**Builder** (`workflow-version-step-operations.workspace-service.ts`)
- Creating an AI step writes `{ instructions: '', prompt: '' }` and creates no agent. Validation reports `AI_AGENT_MISSING_PROMPT` until the prompt is filled, because the prompt is the run's only message.
- Creating an AI step with `defaultSettings.input.agentId` builds an agent step for that agent.
- Cloning, drafting and deleting a step only copy or delete the hidden agent a legacy step owns (an `isSystem` agent). This keeps existing steps working until the migration PR inlines them, and the runtime never branches on migration state.
- A reusable agent that a step runs is kept as is and is never deleted with the step.
- A step without an agent is cloned as a plain copy.

**Front** (`ai-agent-action/`)
- An inline step edits its config on the step itself:
  - a new **Instructions** field;
  - the model;
  - web search.
- Its prompt field says it is required.
- Its Permissions tab edits `settings.input.scope` by object and permission flag universal identifiers, instead of creating and assigning a role.
  - It lists the scope's all-object grants, which can be removed.

**Tools**

## What changed

The Stage becomes a 3D town that is your codebase, so someone who does not read code can see what Claude is doing to their project and learn what each part is.

- **The town is the project.** A shop on the main street for each page, an office for server code, a warehouse for data, a building per outside service that fits what it does (a bank for Stripe, a power station for hosting, a guard house for login, a second warehouse for a hosted database), a safe for secret settings, a supply yard for packages, an archive for git. Existing projects open with their town already standing: on session start the server scans the project folder once, by file names only.
- **It grows from what really happened.** Empty lot, dig, foundation, bricks, concrete, walls and paint, neighbours, neighbourhood, live town. A change stays grey until a test or build passes, a failure smokes until it is fixed, shops light up while a dev server runs.
- **Claude's steps play as work** at the building they touched, with the step's caption: blueprint for a read, bricks for a new file, scaffolding or paint for an edit, a delivery for an install, the inspector for tests, a mixer for a build, a photo for a commit, trucks for push and pull, a ribbon for a deploy. Overlays for failed, stopped by you, fixed, and waiting on you. Bursts fold together and the camera zooms out over busy buildings.
- **Tap anything for a concept card**: an analogy, then on Go deeper what it really is, the real files in this project, the steps that touched them, related ideas, and a Glossary link. Every building is also in an accessible list for keyboards and screen readers.
- **Timeline** along the bottom replaces the step drawer on the Stage: a band per request, a mark per step coloured by outcome; scrub or use the arrow keys to see the town as it stood.
- **Set up GitHub safely** on the archive's card: a checklist (repo, .gitignore covering secrets, README, GitHub remote, pushed) with why each matters, and a request to copy into Claude Code. Sidecar never runs it.
- **Layout C, wide screens**: no 1440px cap, 8px gutters; town fills the Stage, cards on the right, timeline at the bottom.
- **Settings > Motion**: follow the OS, less motion, or full motion. Dark theme is the town at dusk.

No model calls anywhere in this feature; scenes and cards come from rules and fixed copy.

## Why

The old Stage drew the same fixed blocks every time and did not explain what the steps meant. The aim is to teach people what is happening in their codebase, with an analogy that always matches the real step.

## Notes for review (@darshjoshi)

Hi Darsh, this one is big, so here is where to look first:

1. **The scan and privacy**: `packages/server/src/scan.ts`. Names only, plus `package.json`, `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `.gitignore` and `.git/config` for the remote. Never opens `.env` or any other file, skips `node_modules`, build output and ignored paths, stops at 5000 files, and skips a session started in the home folder or at a filesystem root. Runs once per session off the event path (`pipeline.ts`), stored in a new `baselines` table, served at `GET /api/sessions/:id/baseline` (null until ready). This is the part I would most like a second pair of eyes on.
2. **The rules**: everything the town decides is pure and tested in `packages/shared/src/city/` (`town.ts`, `scenes.ts`, `pacing.ts`, `concepts.ts`, `github.ts`). `project-map.ts` gains an `existing` state for scanned files; `recap.ts` now counts only changed and failed parts so existing ones never read as work done. `serverUrl` (recap) and `covers` (story) are exported so the town shares their rules.
3. **The renderer**: `apps/web/src/city/` (three.js 0.186.1, pinned). It only draws what the shared rules decide, builds each building once, merges meshes per material, frees GPU memory and the WebGL context on unmount, and loads in its own chunk. `apps/web/city-gallery.html` is a dev-only page under `vite` to see every stage (`?stage=N`, `?dark`) and every scene (`?scenes`).
4. **What was left behind**: `StoryDrawer`, `Legend`, `stage.ts` and the ui-kit SVG stage are no longer used by the Stage tab but are still in the tree (the kit gallery still uses the SVG stage). Happy to remove them here or in a follow-up, your call.
5. **Known gaps** (follow-ups, not in this PR): the foreman walking past an existing project's buildings on first view; an empty archive lot with a sign when there is no repo; a warning tag on the safe when a secret file is not in .gitignore; relative `../` paths can still become buildings; only the top `.gitignore` is read; cards describe the end of the session while replaying.

A fresh full-branch review already ran; its eight important findings are fixed in `3ad78da` and `378adf8` (live failure and waiting overlays, scrubbing during a scene, WebGL context leak, per-step cost on big projects, reset on session switch, home-folder scan, GitHub checklist staying stale, and `rm -rf build` counting as a passing check).

## How I verified it

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` (1232 tests)
- [x] `pnpm build` and `pnpm smoke`, plus `pnpm test:mod` (18) and `pnpm e2e` (25, zero tokens, no console errors)
- [ ] Ran Claude Code with `claude --plugin-dir ./plugin` and watched the change in the workstation. Not yet: I replayed the bench's build-stripe-app session into a local server pointed at this repo instead, and checked light and dark by eye.

## Checklist

- [ ] One change per pull request. This is one feature, but a large one (21 commits, each with its own tests); happy to split if you prefer.
- [x] Conventional commit messages, no em dashes
- [x] Hooks still exit 0 and stay fast, whatever happens (the scan never runs in a hook)
- [x] Anything new that reaches the model or the database is scrubbed first (the scan stores names only; nothing new reaches the model)
- [x] Model text is rendered as plain text, never as HTML
- [x] Snapshots updated only for an intentional visual change (none changed)
- [x] No secrets, and nothing personal in fixtures or screenshots
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated
